chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Isḥāq ibn Yashkur al-Kahili from al-Ḥakam from Anas who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever places a lamp in one of the mosques of Allah, the angels and the bearers of the Throne will continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as there is light from that lamp in the mosque.'

key_terms.أَسْرَجَ: placed a lamp / equipped with a lamp

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for placing a lamp in a mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith underscores the virtue of enhancing the physical and spiritual atmosphere of mosques, linking material charity to continuous divine intercession. It specifically highlights the honor bestowed upon the benefactor by the highest celestial beings—the angels and the bearers of the Throne (Hamlat al-Arsh)—emphasizing the mosque as a locus of cosmic worship. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on maintaining the sanctity and comfort of communal prayer spaces as an act of enduring devotion.
